clue.text: Hangs about to attend to sheep

indicators.note: the word for hangs goes round the word for attend to, wrapping it

parts.note: to hang something is to sling it
to attend to a speaker is to hear them

explanation.surface: Someone loiters about, ready to look after the flock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hangs about' reads as loitering, but 'Hangs' is a verb meaning slings and 'about' is the container signal wrapping the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Shearlings are young sheep that have been shorn once, so the word names the animals themselves.

clue.text: Calm retort

explanation.definitionFit: Still air is calm, and a still is a distilling vessel, which is what a retort is in a laboratory.

clue.text: Day-long back-exercises border on real craziness

indicators.note: placed before the exercises, this asks for the gym abbreviation to be read backwards

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises
a hem is the border of a garment

indicators.note: craziness says the word real is to be scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone's day-long back workout verges on madness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the gym abbreviation round and 'craziness' scrambles the last word; 'on' is a link. 'Day-long' looks like a description of the exercises, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ephemeral literally lasts only a day, from the Greek for a single day, hence short-lived.

clue.text: "A — in a cage puts all Heaven in a rage" (Blake)

definitions.text: "A — in a cage puts all Heaven in a rage" (Blake)

parts.words: "A — in a cage puts all Heaven in a rage" (Blake)
parts.note: a line from William Blake's Auguries of Innocence with the name of a caged songbird left blank, to be filled in

explanation.surface: A quotation from Blake with its caged bird missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The line comes from Blake's poem Auguries of Innocence; the blank is the familiar British garden bird with an orange-red chest.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing words name the bird in Blake's couplet, the common European songbird with a red front.

clue.text: In time this will get severe

parts.note: taken as written
in grammar a tense is the form of a verb showing time

explanation.surface: Given time, this will turn harsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In time' reads as 'eventually', but split it: IN plus a grammatical time, a tense. 'this will get' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense pain or cold is extreme, as severe weather or pain is.

clue.text: The common man carrying a member's robe

indicators.note: one word holding another inside it, as a bearer carries a load

parts.note: a gent is an ordinary man, the familiar word for a gentleman
an arm is a limb, and member is an old word for a limb

explanation.surface: An ordinary chap wears the robe belonging to a club member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' signals the container; 'member' looks like a club member, but it is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: A robe is a loose item of clothing, and a garment is any article of clothing.

clue.text: Just getting light

explanation.definitionFit: A just decision is fair, and fair hair or skin is pale and light in colour.

clue.text: Eager to have a drink about four

indicators.note: the drink goes round the numeral, enclosing it

parts.note: ale is beer, a drink
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone keen to have a drink at about four o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container, after the opening A. 'about four' looks like a time of day.
explanation.definitionFit: To be alive to something is to be keenly aware and responsive, so eager and lively.

clue.text: Gun brought up with a mount for the governor

indicators.note: in a down clue the weapon's name is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a Luger is a German pistol
a tor is a rocky hill, a mount

explanation.surface: A gun is raised beside a horse as the governor arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns LUGER into REGUL. 'mount' suggests a horse but means a hill; a governor here is a device that controls speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A governor in engineering is a mechanism that keeps speed steady, which is exactly what a regulator does.

clue.text: Capital news!

parts.note: the four letters N, E, W, S, written as capitals, are the abbreviations for the four main compass directions

explanation.surface: Exciting headlines from the city.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'news' in capital letters is N, E, W, S: north, east, west and south.
explanation.definitionFit: North, east, south and west are the main directions on a compass, whose initials spell news.

clue.text: Tenant dressed like a monk

explanation.definitionFit: To tenant a house is to occupy or live in it, and a monk wears a habit, so he is in one.

clue.text: The place of the bibliophile?

parts.note: a book lover's favourite activity is also the name of an English town, a place

explanation.surface: Where would a book lover live?
explanation.walkthrough: Reading is a large town west of London, and also what a lover of books does.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in Berkshire shares its name with the act of looking through books, the bibliophile's pastime.

clue.text: Though calm, ennui concealed brightness

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are disguised, their true order concealed in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Even a calm boredom couldn't hide someone's brilliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealed' rearranges CALM ENNUI. 'Though' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Luminance is the measured intensity of light given off by a surface, its brightness.

clue.text: Figure on a water-supply, so stay

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a figure
a well supplies water

explanation.surface: Someone sees a number on the village water-supply and decides to remain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' joins D to WELL; in an across clue it places the figure first.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to live or remain there, to stay.

clue.text: Short ton — Irish?

parts.note: Erse is the Gaelic language of Ireland

explanation.surface: Is a short ton an Irish unit of weight?
explanation.walkthrough: A short ton is a real American unit, which makes 'Short' look part of the phrase rather than the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A terse reply is brief and curt, a short one.

clue.text: Chance it perhaps — the trainee is industrial

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters could stand in another order

parts.note: L is the learner plate on a British learner driver's car

explanation.surface: Take a chance on an industrial trainee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges CHANCE IT into TECHNICA, followed by L. L for learner comes from British L-plates.
explanation.definitionFit: Technical and industrial both describe practical, applied skills such as those taught at a technical college.

clue.text: Former nurse and social worker displayed heraldically

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife
to nurse someone is to tend them
the ant is a social insect, and many ants are workers

explanation.surface: A one-time nurse and a social worker are pictured on a coat of arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' suggests a caseworker, but it is an ant, the social insect.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry an extendant creature is shown spread out, its limbs stretched wide on the shield.

clue.text: Change a number at one point in dispute

parts.note: to change something is to alter it
C is the Roman numeral for 100
taken as written
E, east, is one point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone changes a figure at one stage in an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' means a compass point, here east.
explanation.definitionFit: To altercate is to quarrel noisily, to argue or wrangle.

clue.text: Have a party and let care be set loose

indicators.note: the words are freed from their order and so rearranged

explanation.surface: Let the worries go and have a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set loose' rearranges LET CARE BE.
explanation.definitionFit: To celebrate is to mark an occasion with festivity, which having a party does.

clue.text: Climbs, since little money's needed

parts.note: as can mean since, as in 'as it rained'
cents are small coins, a little money

explanation.surface: Climbing, since it costs little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed' and the apostrophe are link material joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascents are climbs up a hill or mountain.

clue.text: Honour among gentlemen noblesse oblige

indicators.note: the answer sits among the letters of the words, across the gap

explanation.surface: Honour among gentlemen is a matter of noble obligation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' signals the run inside gentlemEN NOBLEsse; 'oblige' is surface padding. Noblesse oblige is the French idea that rank brings duties.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble someone is to raise them to the nobility, conferring an honour on them.

clue.text: Fed in different ways subsequently

indicators.note: the word for fed goes inside the pair of direction letters

parts.note: L and R, left and right, are two different directions or ways
fed is ate, as in 'they ate early'

explanation.surface: Someone is fed in various ways afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed' looks like the definition but gives ATE; L and R stand for left and right.
explanation.definitionFit: Later means at a time after this, subsequently.

clue.text: Bond readily returned a key taken

indicators.note: the word for readily is turned back on itself

parts.note: soon can mean readily or willingly, as in 'I'd as soon go'
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone's bond is quickly returned once a key has been taken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns SOON into NOOS. Soon in the sense of readily survives in 'I would sooner'.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop of rope that ties or binds, so a bond.

clue.text: Girl from the Pacific branch

explanation.definitionFit: Olive is a girl's name, and an olive branch is a peaceful offering, pacific meaning peace-making.

clue.text: The anti-hunt crowd

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
to course is to hunt hares with hounds

explanation.surface: The protesters against hunting gather in a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The anti-hunt' reads as campaigners against field sports; split it into two words, against plus hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: A concourse is a large gathering of people, a crowd or throng.

clue.text: Unknown character cutting tree up for use

indicators.note: the letter cuts into the word, splitting it
in a down clue the word for tree is read upwards

parts.note: x is the classic unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: Some unknown person cuts a tree upward for its timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TREE into EERT, and 'cutting' puts X into it.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert strength is to use it, bring it into action.

clue.text: Colour of lake

parts.note: lake is a pigment, and one deep red pigment of that kind gives its name to a shade

explanation.surface: What shade is the lake?
explanation.walkthrough: Lake here is a painter's pigment, not water; the crimson lake pigment is a deep red.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimson lake is a traditional red pigment, so the colour named for it is a deep red.

clue.text: Dressing makes musicians look older

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
to age is to grow or look older

explanation.surface: Getting dressed up makes the musicians look older.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing' suggests clothes or salad, but it is a wound dressing. 'makes' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandage is a strip of material used as a dressing for a wound.

clue.text: Right out of line

indicators.note: the letters are knocked out of line, out of their order

explanation.surface: It's not right to step out of line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' rearranges LINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lien is a legal right to keep someone's property until a debt is paid.

clue.text: Fools people in a good man's charge

parts.note: asses are fools

indicators.note: people go inside the abbreviation for a saint

parts.note: ST, saint, is a good man
men are people

explanation.surface: Fools and people are in a good man's care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container. 'charge' reads as care but means a levy.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessment is a sum levied or charged, such as a tax.
